es.summary: La naloxona es un antagonista de los receptores mu opioides que revierte rápidamente la depresión respiratoria por sobredosis de opioides.
key_points: Se administra por vía intranasal, intramuscular o intravenosa en emergencias.
Su efecto dura 30‑90 minutos, por lo que pueden requerirse dosis repetidas.
Puede precipitar síndrome de abstinencia aguda en pacientes dependientes.
Se debe monitorizar la respiración y la saturación de O₂ continuamente.
No sustituye la atención médica de urgencia; siempre se debe llamar a EMS.

mechanism: Bloquea competitivamente los receptores mu opioides, impidiendo la unión del opioide.
Invierte la inhibición del centro respiratorio en el tronco encefálico.
No posee actividad agonista; su acción es puramente antagonista.
indications: Tratamiento de emergencia de sobredosis conocida o sospechada de opioides.
Reversión de depresión respiratoria y del SNC por opioides.
Uso profiláctico en pacientes con alto riesgo de sobredosis (ej. terapia de sustitución).
contraindications: Hipersensibilidad conocida a la naloxona o a cualquiera de sus excipientes.
adverse_effects: Síndrome de abstinencia aguda (dolor abdominal, diarrea, temblores) – serio.
Depresión respiratoria recurrente cuando el opioide persiste – serio.
interactions: Opioides agonistas pueden reducir la duración del efecto de la naloxona.
Benzodiacepinas y otros depresores del SNC pueden mantener depresión respiratoria.
Uso concomitante con buprenorfina puede precipitar abstinencia severa.
nursing_care: Evaluar vía aérea, frecuencia respiratoria y nivel de conciencia antes de administrar.
Administrar la dosis recomendada (ej. 2 mg spray nasal) y observar respuesta en 2‑5 min.
Monitorear signos vitales, saturación de O₂ y posible re‑depresión respiratoria.
Repetir dosis cada 2‑3 min si la depresión persiste, usando un nuevo dispositivo.
Notificar al médico inmediatamente después de la primera dosis y cada repetición.
patient_teaching: Mantener el kit de naloxona en un lugar accesible y enseñar su uso correcto.
Llamar a emergencias (119) después de la administración, aun si la respiración mejora.
Informar que pueden presentarse síntomas de abstinencia (náuseas, temblores).
No reutilizar el dispositivo; desechar según indicaciones del fabricante.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Hidratación adecuada: ingesta de líquidos ≥1500 mL/día
Equilibrio electrolítico: Na⁺ 135‑145 mEq/L y K⁺ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L

interventions.action: Evaluar peso y signos de deshidratación antes y después de la administración.
interventions.rationale: Detectar pérdida de líquidos por vómitos o sudoración.

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada 4 horas.
interventions.rationale: Facilita el control del balance hídrico.

interventions.action: Ofrecer líquidos claros cada 30 min si el paciente está alerta y sin riesgo de aspiración.
interventions.rationale: Previene el déficit de volumen y mantiene la perfusión tisular.

interventions.action: Monitorear electrolitos (Na⁺, K⁺) al menos 24 h después de la dosis.
interventions.rationale: Identificar desequilibrios derivados de pérdidas gastrointestinales.

interventions.action: Notificar al médico si se observa hipotensión, taquicardia o signos de deshidratación severa.
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención temprana y ajuste de terapia.

en.summary: Naloxone is an opioid mu receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses respiratory depression caused by opioid overdose.
key_points: Administered intranasally, intramuscularly, or intravenously in emergencies.
Its effect lasts 30‑90 minutes, so repeat doses may be required.
It can precipitate acute withdrawal in opioid‑dependent patients.
Respiration and O₂ saturation must be continuously monitored.
It does not replace emergency medical care; EMS should always be called.

mechanism: Competes for mu opioid receptors, blocking opioid binding.
Reverses inhibition of the respiratory center in the brainstem.
Has no agonist activity; its action is purely antagonistic.
indications: Emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose.
Reversal of respiratory and CNS depression from opioids.
Prophylactic use in patients at high risk of overdose (e.g., substitution therapy).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to naloxone or any of its excipients.
adverse_effects: Acute withdrawal syndrome (abdominal pain, diarrhea, tremors) – serious.
Recurrent respiratory depression when the opioid persists – serious.
interactions: Opioid agonists can shorten naloxone’s duration of action.
Benzodiazepines and other CNS depressants may maintain respiratory depression.
Concurrent use with buprenorphine can precipitate severe withdrawal.
nursing_care: Assess airway, respiratory rate, and level of consciousness before administration.
Give the recommended dose (e.g., 2 mg intranasal spray) and observe response in 2‑5 min.
Monitor vital signs, O₂ saturation, and possible re‑depression of respiration.
Repeat dose every 2‑3 min if depression persists, using a new device.
Notify the physician immediately after the first dose and each repeat.
patient_teaching: Keep the naloxone kit in an accessible place and teach proper use.
Call emergency services (119) after administration, even if breathing improves.
Inform that withdrawal symptoms (nausea, tremors) may occur.
Do not reuse the device; discard per manufacturer instructions.

outcomes: Electrolyte balance: Na⁺ 135‑145 mEq/L and K⁺ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L

interventions.action: Assess weight and signs of dehydration before and after administration.
interventions.rationale: Detect fluid loss from vomiting or sweating.

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output every 4 hours.
Offer clear fluids every 30 min if the patient is alert and at low aspiration risk.
interventions.rationale: Prevents volume deficit and maintains tissue perfusion.

interventions.action: Monitor electrolytes (Na⁺, K⁺) at least 24 h after the dose.
Notify the physician if hypotension, tachycardia, or severe dehydration signs appear.
interventions.rationale: Allows early intervention and therapy adjustment.

summary.0.quote: Naloxone is the prototypical mu opioid receptor antagonist used to rapidly reverse the life-threatening effects of opioid overdose.

key_points.0.quote: Naloxone can be given intravenously, intramuscularly, or intranasally.

key_points.1.quote: Importantly, naloxone has a duration of action of only approximately 20–30 minutes.

key_points.2.quote: Use in patients who are opioid dependent may precipitate opioid withdrawal.

key_points.4.quote: Always seek emergency medical assistance in the event of a suspected, potentially life-threatening opioid emergency after administration of the first dose of Naloxone HCl Nasal Spray.

sections.indications.0.quote: Naloxone HCl Nasal Spray is indicated for the emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose, as manifested by respiratory and/or central nervous system depression.

sections.indications.1.quote: Naloxone HCl Nasal Spray is indicated for the emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose, as manifested by respiratory and/or central nervous system depression.

sections.contraindications.0.quote: Naloxone HCl Nasal Spray is contraindicated in patients known to be hypersensitive to naloxone hydrochloride or to any of the other ingredients.

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Abrupt postoperative reversal of opioid depression after using naloxone hydrochloride may result in nausea, vomiting, sweating, tremulousness, tachycardia, hypotension, hypertension, seizures, ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation, pulmonary edema, and cardiac arrest.

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Signs and symptoms have included: body aches, fever, sweating, runny nose, sneezing, piloerection, yawning, weakness, shivering or trembling, nervousness, restlessness or irritability, diarrhea, nausea or vomiting, abdominal cramps, increased blood pressure, tachycardia.

sections.adverse_effects.3.quote: The duration of action of most opioids may exceed that of Naloxone HCl Nasal Spray resulting in a return of respiratory and/or central nervous system depression after an initial improvement in symptoms.

sections.interactions.1.quote: Concomitant use of opioids with benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants, including alcohol, may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: If additional Naloxone HCl Nasal Sprays are available, Steps 2 through 6 may be repeated every 2 to 3 minutes until the person responds or emergency medical help is received.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: Turn patient on their side as shown in the Instructions for Use and call for emergency medical assistance immediately after administration of the first dose of Naloxone HCl Nasal Spray.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Ensure that naloxone is readily available in the event of opioid toxicity or overdose.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Gastrointestinal effects of opioid withdrawal include severe abdominal cramping, diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting.
